debutant.name: The Mirror
debutant.desc: Two players face each other. One makes slow movements, the other mirrors them exactly. Speed up gradually. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: The Chairs
debutant.desc: One team has 30s to build a structure out of chairs. Another team has 40s to prepare an improv based on that structure. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: The Eulogy
debutant.desc: Each player improvises a tribute speech for their pet. Solemn tone, funny, or both. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: Collective Story
debutant.desc: In a circle, one word each. The story is built collectively, with no hesitation and no going back.

debutant.name: Embody the Theme
debutant.desc: The group moves around, a leader calls out a theme (museum, pyramids...). The group recreates it immediately. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: Odd Conversation
debutant.desc: Two players improvise an offbeat situation: a bird explaining trees to another bird, a flea arguing with a dog. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: Yes, and...
debutant.desc: Every offer is accepted and built on. The golden rule of improv according to InFamily: never block.

debutant.name: The Imaginary Object
debutant.desc: One player handles an invisible object. The others guess what it is and send it back with a new use added.

debutant.name: The Drunk Guy
debutant.desc: An audience member (or an actor) plays the "drunk guy", interrupting the scene with absurd suggestions the improvisers must work in to move the story forward.

debutant.name: Question Circle
debutant.desc: One player stands in the middle of the circle. The others fire questions at them. They answer each one precisely. (Dramaction)

debutant.name: Emotions on Cue
debutant.desc: The leader calls out an emotion. The players switch to it instantly and justify it on stage.

debutant.name: The Human Machine
debutant.desc: One by one, players step in and add a repeating gesture/sound. The machine builds itself organically.

debutant.name: ABC
debutant.desc: A scene where each line starts with the next letter of the alphabet. A, B, C... all the way to Z.

debutant.name: The Bus
debutant.desc: A bus stop. At each arrival, a new character gets on with their own world. The scene shifts every time.

debutant.name: Pantomime
debutant.desc: A scene played entirely in mime from a given theme. (Dramaction)

debutant.name: Three Characters
debutant.desc: Three players enter and establish their character in under 30 seconds, through posture and voice alone.

debutant.name: Passing the Emotion
debutant.desc: One player silently passes an emotion to their neighbour through a gesture, who passes it on in turn. (Dramaction)

debutant.name: Freeze
debutant.desc: Two players improvise starting from a frozen pose. At any moment, another claps to freeze the scene and replace a player. (Impro-Exo)

debutant.name: Beginning-Middle-End in 30s
debutant.desc: Start an improv, shift the stakes, and wrap it up — all in 30 seconds flat. (Impro-Exo)

debutant.name: Shifting-Emotion Conversation
debutant.desc: A conversation between two players. Every 1-2 minutes, a leader shouts out an emotion. The players switch. (MentorShow)

debutant.name: Mixed
debutant.desc: All the players of the troupe come on together and play the theme without splitting into teams. (Match category, adapted)

debutant.name: Compared
debutant.desc: Two subgroups of the troupe play the same prompt one after the other. The 2nd version must stand apart from the 1st. (Match category, adapted)

debutant.name: Free Compared
debutant.desc: Two subgroups play the same theme one after the other, with no constraint on form. Total freedom. (Match category, adapted)

debutant.name: Mixed with Prop
debutant.desc: A required object must be central to the collective improv. The whole troupe makes it their own on stage. (Match category, adapted)

confirme.name: Pause-Resume
confirme.desc: The leader stops the scene, changes one element (place, era, status), and has it resume.

confirme.name: Three Required Words
confirme.desc: Three words drawn at random must be worked naturally into the scene.

confirme.name: Status
confirme.desc: Each character has a hidden social status (1 to 10). The audience has to guess it.

confirme.name: Dubbing
confirme.desc: Two players mime, two others speak for them from off the stage.

confirme.name: Expert Panel
confirme.desc: A panel of experts on an absurd subject answers the audience's questions in complete seriousness.

confirme.name: Last word, first word
confirme.desc: Each line must begin with the last word of the previous one.

confirme.name: Backwards Story
confirme.desc: Tell a story starting from the end and working back scene by scene.

confirme.name: Mixed Genres
confirme.desc: The leader switches genre every 30 seconds (western, crime, romance, horror...).

confirme.name: Triple Status
confirme.desc: Each character has a secret, a goal and an obstacle. All three come out during the scene.

confirme.name: Reversed Scene
confirme.desc: Start at the climax and work back to the moment the characters first met.

confirme.name: The Off-Key Choir
confirme.desc: A choir on stage — one member is off-key or out of time. All the drama comes from them. (Wikiversité)

confirme.name: Actors in the Wings
confirme.desc: A scene plays out in the wings while the 'show' goes on onstage. Mise en abyme. (Wikiversité)

confirme.name: The Stuck Elevator
confirme.desc: An extremely confined space, several characters, a forced huis clos. A classic. (Wikiversité)

confirme.name: The Teachers' Meeting
confirme.desc: A staff meeting where every teacher has a hidden agenda and a favourite pupil.

confirme.name: Rewind
confirme.desc: At a key moment, a player claps. The scene jumps back 1 minute and replays differently.

confirme.name: The Drawn Character
confirme.desc: Each player draws a character type (clown, seducer, paranoiac) and must play it without naming it.

confirme.name: Mixed, In the Style Of
confirme.desc: Everyone plays the theme in an imposed author's style or genre: Molière, Audiard, film noir... (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: Compared, In the Style Of
confirme.desc: Two sub-groups play the same theme one after the other in the imposed style, each in their own way. (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: Wordless Mixed
confirme.desc: Not a word spoken: the collective staging alone tells the story. Extreme focus. (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: Wordless with Musical Support
confirme.desc: A silent impro, but the storytelling is strictly shaped by the imposed musical atmosphere. (Dramaction)

confirme.name: Compared with Constraint
confirme.desc: Two sub-groups play the same theme one after the other, each with a different constraint drawn at random. (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: No Theme, No Caucus
confirme.desc: No theme announced, no caucus. Pure on-the-spot invention. (Dramaction)

confirme.name: Leapfrog
confirme.desc: Four different impros, one theme per impro. The 1st with one player, then one more player is added for each impro that follows. (Dramaction)

confirme.name: Sensory
confirme.desc: One of the five senses of one improviser is stimulated during the scene. That sensation must feed the whole story. (Dramaction)

expert.name: The Harold
expert.desc: Long form: three parallel scenes interweave, answer and feed each other. Del Close format.

expert.name: The Fireball
expert.desc: All the players on stage. At each high point, a duo breaks away for a mini-scene, then returns to the group.

expert.name: Sung Improvisation
expert.desc: A scene entirely sung, with improvised melody, rhymes and a verse/chorus structure.

expert.name: The Shared Monologue
expert.desc: A long monologue is picked up by each player in turn, who distorts and enriches it while playing the same character.

expert.name: 20-Minute Free Form
expert.desc: A single scene, twenty minutes, with no interruption and no switch. Holding up an entire world.

expert.name: Impro Opera
expert.desc: Sung recitatives and arias in alternation, a fully improvised libretto, operatic voices.

expert.name: The Pirandello Mirror
expert.desc: The characters realise they are being improvised... but have to carry on with the scene anyway.

expert.name: Scene in Two Movements
expert.desc: A scene is played, then replayed ten years later with the logical consequences of the first.

expert.name: Silent Improvisation
expert.desc: A 15-minute show, entirely without words, with a clear plot that gets resolved.

expert.name: Theatre Within the Theatre
expert.desc: The characters in turn improvise a play inside the scene. Three layers of fiction stacked on top of each other.

expert.name: The House (Del Close)
expert.desc: A long form where each scene opens themes that the following ones pick up and deepen.

expert.name: The Deconstructed
expert.desc: A single scene is played, then taken apart and started over from several narrative angles.

expert.name: Chekhovian
expert.desc: Long form in the manner of Chekhov: no climax, characters who keep missing each other, inaction as the engine.

expert.name: Beckettian
expert.desc: Absurdist long form: inhabited silences, waiting, language draining itself. In the vein of Waiting for Godot.

expert.name: Sung mixed
expert.desc: An impro sung entirely or partly by the whole troupe, with melodies and lyrics improvised collectively. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: Sung compared
expert.desc: Two sub-groups perform their sung version of the same theme one after the other. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: Rhymed mixed
expert.desc: Every line rhymes. Octosyllables or alexandrines depending on level. The whole troupe holds the metre. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: Rhymed compared
expert.desc: Two sub-groups deliver their rhymed version of the theme one after the other. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: Videoway
expert.desc: A mixed impro with four TV channels (F1-F4), each channel a different content. The leader jumps from one channel to another in no set order. (Dramaction)

expert.name: Thesis mixed
expert.desc: The collective impro must argue a philosophical thesis announced in advance.

debutant.name: Single improv
debutant.desc: One team plays, the other waits. The classic form of the LNI impro match.

debutant.name: Mixed improv
debutant.desc: Both teams play together in the same impro, with equal numbers on each side.

debutant.name: Compared improv
debutant.desc: Each team plays the same brief in turn. The audience compares and votes.

debutant.name: Wordless mixed
debutant.desc: Both teams together, but in absolute silence for the whole scene.

debutant.name: Sung compared
debutant.desc: Each team plays the theme, working in at least one sung passage.

debutant.name: Compared with a prop
debutant.desc: An imposed prop must be central. Each team uses it its own way.

confirme.name: In the style of
confirme.desc: An imposed author or genre style: Molière, Audiard, film noir... (Classic LNI category)

confirme.name: Mixed with a prop
confirme.desc: An imposed object must be central to the impro. The two teams negotiate it on stage.

confirme.name: Compared with a constraint
confirme.desc: Each team plays the theme with a different randomly drawn constraint.

confirme.name: Mixed with an imposed character
confirme.desc: An imposed character type must appear within the first minute.

confirme.name: Backwards improv
confirme.desc: The team must play the scene starting from the end and working back.

confirme.name: Mixed in full sentences
confirme.desc: Players may only speak in whole, complete sentences — no interrupting.

confirme.name: Rhymed compared
confirme.desc: Every line must rhyme (octosyllables or rhyming couplets).

confirme.name: Silent compared
confirme.desc: Not a word spoken: gesture and expression alone tell the story.

expert.name: Sung and danced
expert.desc: A mini-musical: improvised dialogue, songs and choreography in alternation. Broadway impro style.

expert.name: In the style of + period
expert.desc: An author's style AND a historical period, both imposed. Both must be readable from the first entrance.

expert.name: Mixed in alexandrines
expert.desc: Every line in alexandrines (12 syllables), in couplets or alternating rhyme. Classical level.

expert.name: Compared silent + sound effects
expert.desc: One team plays silently, the other in sound effects only. Same theme, opposite readings.

expert.name: No hero
expert.desc: The impro must work with no identifiable lead character. Pure ensemble playing.

expert.name: Thesis improv
expert.desc: The impro must argue a philosophical thesis announced in advance by the referee.

expert.name: In the style of Chekhov
expert.desc: Late-19th-century Russian style: aristocratic boredom, samovars, loaded silences, monologues.

expert.name: Time backpedal
expert.desc: The scene moves forward then rewinds every 30 seconds. A dizzying loop.

debutant: Walking in a circle the entire time
Every other line must be sung
confirme: In the style of 1940s film noir
In slow motion from start to finish
In fast forward from start to finish
Alternating English and an invented language
In the style of an animated cartoon
expert: Time-rewind: scene moves forward then rewinds every 30s
Multiple voices: each character played by 2 actors at once
External narration that contradicts the action
Palindromic: scene must be playable in reverse
An entirely invented but consistent language

debutant: With a forced phrase to slip in
expert: With a character who knows it is fiction

debutant: The TV news from another planet
An interrogation about a tiny matter
confirme: A cat speaking to its owner
The train journey with no destination
The hotel forgotten by all maps
The dream that returns every night
Two strangers in a stuck elevator
The photo we shouldn't have seen
The house that changes at night
The station of souls in transit
The teachers' meeting about one student
The lesson that makes no sense
Darth Vader calls to break up
expert: The final conversation between God and Devil
The testament of a dead language
The final performance at the Globe
The seven deadly sins at dinner
The dream within the dream within the dream
The tightrope walker between two worlds
Three sisters who'll never reach Moscow
The night watchman of forgotten things
The last translator of the useless

categories.name: Mixed
categories.desc: Both teams play together, balanced numbers, on the same theme.

categories.name: Compared
categories.desc: Each team plays the same prompt in turn. Audience compares and votes.

categories.name: In the manner of
categories.desc: Style or genre imposed (Shakespeare, noir, Tarantino...).

categories.name: Compared in the manner of
categories.desc: Each team plays the theme in the imposed style, in its own way.

categories.name: Compared sung
categories.desc: Each team offers its own sung version of the same theme.

categories.name: Silent
categories.desc: No spoken word: only gesture tells the story.

categories.name: Silent with music
categories.desc: Mute scene, but writing rigorously shaped by an imposed musical mood.

categories.name: Rhymed
categories.desc: All lines must rhyme. Couplets or alexandrines depending on level.

categories.name: Compared rhymed
categories.desc: Each team delivers its own rhymed version of the theme.

categories.name: With prop
categories.desc: An imposed object must be central.

categories.name: Forced constraint
categories.desc: A constraint drawn at random applies to one or both teams.

categories.name: No theme, no caucus
categories.desc: No theme announced, no preparation time. Pure on-the-spot invention.

categories.name: Leapfrog
categories.desc: Four different improvs, one theme each. The first with one player; one player added each round.

categories.name: Videoway
categories.desc: Mixed with 4 TV channels (F1-F4), different content per channel. Referee jumps between channels at will.

categories.name: Sensory
categories.desc: One sense of one improviser is stimulated. That sensation must shape the entire scene.

categories.name: Thesis
categories.desc: Improvisation must defend a philosophical thesis announced in advance.

categories.name: Free
categories.desc: No formal constraint, just the theme. Total freedom of treatment.
